title: Temporal cliques admit linear spanners
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the theorem that every temporal clique on n vertices admits a temporal spanner with at most 7n edges. A temporal clique is the complete graph on a finite vertex set whose edges carry natural-number time labels, locally injective (two edges sharing an endpoint have distinct labels); a temporal spanner is a set of edges in which every vertex reaches every other one by a journey with non-decreasing labels. The result and its proof are due to Júlia Baligács (arXiv:2606.05156, 2026): the dismountability of Carnevale, Casteigts and Corsini (SAND 2025) reduces cliques to extremally matched bi-cliques, which are then covered by simple and extended stars. The compared statements give the explicit bound 7n and the asymptotic O(n) form with a bound function chosen uniformly for all cliques. They use the same definitions as the registered O(n log n) entry. This repository is a thin wrapper: it contains only the statement and the bridge to the temporal-graphs library, the substantive formalization, on which it depends through its lakefile at the commit given below (release alpha-0.2.0 of the library, on its branch prepared for Palomar). The work is supervised by Arnaud Casteigts and Karine Altisen.
